name: Lars Tang
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember cutting my first ham with an old carpenter directing me.” On Wednesday, near Juniper Street, Lars knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I carved the ham years ago. Now my hands shake and the owner's son asked me to teach him where to start.
appearance: Lars has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for salt-and-pepper curls. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. In conversation Lars rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Lars has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To teach the butcher's son the first proper slice.
family: Mika Tsai is Lars’s younger cousin. Lars offers the first invitation. Mika gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Two birthdays in one ward*, Mika says, “I was discharged that morning and returned as a visitor in my own coat.”
connections: Gerard Garza. One exchange returns a coat, another passes down the old knowledge of carving.
